summary: Experimental glirastes/server/stt-local transcribes browser recordings in your own Node server (Parakeet TDT 0.6b v3 int8 via sherpa-onnx), through a new transcribe option on createRecordingTranscriptionHandler and the CLI command glirastes stt pull.
howTo: createRecordingTranscriptionHandler now also takes { transcribe } instead of url: const stt = createLocalTranscriber() from glirastes/server/stt-local (ESM only), then createRecordingTranscriptionHandler({ authorize, transcribe: stt.transcribe }). In this mode the default timeout is 120 s, WAV that is not PCM16 mono 16 kHz answers 415, a full queue (TranscriptionUnavailableError) answers 503, the timeout 504, and a client disconnect 499 without onError. Install the optional peer exactly: npm install sherpa-onnx-node@2.0.1 (linux-x64 2.0.2 does not load on Debian bookworm). Run glirastes stt pull (at image build, into GLIRASTES_MODEL_DIR) to download the sha256-pinned models; nothing is downloaded at runtime. Plan about 2 GB of memory per process, glibc Linux (no Alpine) or macOS arm64, export const runtime = 'nodejs' and serverExternalPackages: ['sherpa-onnx-node', 'glirastes'] in next.config. checkLocalStt() is a model-free deploy readiness check. See docs/local-stt.md.
